answer: Sybil defense uses a protocol-priced deposit: each agent identity locks a fixed amount of the settlement token in escrow until long vesting ends, slashed for duplicate workloads. Because the price is protocol-fixed, a fake cluster costs capital proportional to its size while that capital idles, so expected return turns negative. Each registration writes a signed kernel record binding deposit, operator key and vesting clock, so auditors replay history and catch recycled funds. A second check ties each payout address to one pigment marker, so a lagoon of clones fails when two claim one shade.
